ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r11.claim: الأزواج means kinds or species of everything.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r12.claim: Another account says everything besides God is paired; this possibility points to a singular maker, God, who is beyond opposites and counterparts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r12.anchor: وكونها أزواجا تدل على أنها ممكنة الوجود، ويدل على أن محدثها فرد، وهو الله المنزه عن الضد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r13.claim: By convention, camels are the only livestock ridden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r13.anchor: والأنعام: المعهود أنه لا يركب من الأنعام إلا الإبل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r14.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with its object omitted, meaning what people ride.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r14.anchor: ما: موصولة والعائد محذوف، أي ما يركبونه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r15.claim: The verb ركب is intransitive in relation to its complement here but can take an object directly where the construction otherwise uses في.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r15.anchor: وركب بالنسبة للعلل، ويتعدى بنفسه على المتعدي بوساطة في،

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

NAHHAS:v4p98/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p98/r10.claim: Alladhī is nominative by coordination with the preceding phrase.

NAHHAS:v4p98/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p98/r11.claim: The plural azwāj comes from zawj; the expected plural pattern was avoided because azwuj would make the waw's movement heavy, so the similar form azmān provides an analogy.
NAHHAS:v4p98/r11.anchor: جمع زوج جمع على أفعال وسبيل فعل من غير هذا الجنس أن يجمع على أفعل

NAHHAS:v4p98/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p98/r12.claim: Kullahā is emphasis, though some grammarians call it an adjective; kullahā is used for a large plural and kullahunna for a small one.
NAHHAS:v4p98/r12.anchor: ( كلها ) توكيد ويسميه بعض النحويين صفة وباب كلها الجمع الكثير والجمع القليل كلهن

NAHHAS:v4p98/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p98/r13.claim: If mā is relative, a pronoun is omitted because of the long separation, though masculine or collective feminine agreement could be explicit; if it is a verbal noun, no pronoun is needed.
NAHHAS:v4p98/r13.anchor: إن جعلت ما بمعنى الذي فالضمير محذوف لطول الموسم ولو ظهر الضمير لجاز مما تركبونه

SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r1.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with an omitted object pronoun: ما تركبونه.
SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r1.anchor: " ما " موصولة. وعائدها محذوف أي: ما تركبونه.

SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r2.claim: For ships, ركب takes a preposition, as in 29:65; for other things it is directly transitive, as in 16:8. The direct pattern prevails here, so the relative object is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:43:12/r2.anchor: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك [العنكبوت: 65] وفي غيره بنفسه قال: لتركبوها [النحل: 8] فغلب هنا المتعدي بنفسه على المتعدي بواسطة فلذلك حذف العائد.

ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r2.claim: الأزواج means all classes or kinds; زوج is used in the sense of “kind.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r2.anchor: معناه خلق الأصناف كلها، تقول عندي من كل زوج أي من كل صنف.

ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r3.claim: God created and subjected ships and livestock for people to ride.

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r1.claim: Asad gives the literal sense of azwaj as 'all pairs'.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r1.anchor: Lit., "all pairs". Some commentators regard the term azwaj as synonymous

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r2.speaker: Baghawi, Zamakhsharl, Baydawi, Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r2.claim: These commentators understand azwaj as kinds of things, beings, and phenomena.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r2.anchor: Some commentators regard the term azwaj as synonymous in this context with "kinds" (Baghawi, Zamakhsharl, Baydawi, Ibn Kathir)

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r3.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r3.claim: Tabari reads the phrase as referring to polarity evident throughout creation.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r3.anchor: Others (e.g., Tabari) see in it a reference to the polarity evident in all creation.

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r4.speaker: Ibn 'Abbas
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, as quoted by Razi, takes the phrase to denote opposites generally, such as sweet and sour or male and female.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r4.anchor: Ibn 'Abbas (as quoted by Razi) says that it denotes the concept of opposites in general

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r5.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r5.claim: Razi expands the idea to complementary pairs throughout creation, while God alone has no opposite, likeness, or complement.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r5.anchor: to which Razi adds that everything in creation has its complement, "like high and low, right and left, front and back

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r6.claim: Asad connects this account of pairs to the statement that nothing is comparable to God.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n10/r6.anchor: Hence, the above sentence is an echo of the statement that "there is nothing that could be compared with Him" (112:4).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p661/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p661/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p661/r5.claim: ما تركبون is not a parallel either: if it means ما تركبونه, agreement can proceed from form to sense in ظهوره and return to singular form in its pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p661/r5.anchor: التقدير ما تركبونه فيكون قد حمل أولا على اللفظ ثم على المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r1.claim: ‘Pairs’ means all classes of created things, rather than pairs in the narrower familiar sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r1.anchor: أي أصناف المخلوقات فالزوج هنا بمعنى الصنف لا بمعناه المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the pairs as kinds and varieties, such as sweet and sour, white and black, and male and female.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الأزواج الضروب والأنواع كالحلو والحامض والأبيض والأسود

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r3.claim: Some say everything besides God is paired because it has an opposite, while God alone is free of counterparts; Alusi questions whether this applies universally.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : كل ما سوى الله سبحانه زوج لأنه لا يخلو من المقابل كفوق وتحت

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r4.claim: A possible basis for that view is that God is one in every respect and uncomposed, unlike contingent beings, whether material or immaterial.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r4.anchor: بناه على أن الواجب جل شأنه واحد من جميع الجهات لا تركيب فيه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r5.claim: ‘What you ride’ is a relative clause with omitted referent; ships take a preposition with ‘ride’ while mounts take a direct object, so the direct construction dominates by strength, or animals are preferred over ships.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#2/r5.anchor: فما موصولة والعائد محذوف والركوب بالنظر إلى الفلكي تعدى بواسطة الحرف وهو في

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.claim: God provided ships and livestock for people to ride on land and sea.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.anchor: {وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون} في البر والبحر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r7.claim: الأزواج means all kinds of created things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r7.anchor: ما تركبونه على تغليب المتعدي بنفسه

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r8.claim: The wording generalizes what is ridden by favoring the directly transitive verb; it may also favor animals made for riding over ships made for it, or common over rare usage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r8.anchor: على تغليب المتعدي بنفسه على المتعدي بغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r2.claim: أزواج refers to all complementary kinds and classes, whose members attain full perfection through one another, including plants, animals, and every other created thing; God alone created them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r2.anchor: أي الأصناف المتشاكلة التي لا يكمل شيء منها غاية الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r3.claim: The wording widens the ordinary sense of pairs: it includes the contrasting means of transport that carry people, ships at sea and livestock on land.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r3.anchor: دل على أن المراد ما هو أعم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r4.claim: الفلك denotes large ships used at sea and الأنعام livestock used on land; each is a gift God made for people to ride.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r5.claim: The relative clause omits its understood object pronoun; the direct transitivity of riding livestock takes precedence over the construction with a preposition used for ships.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r5.anchor: وحذف العائد لفهم المعنى تغليبا للمتعدي بنفسه في الأنعام على المتعدي بواسطة في الفلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.claim: The eleven second-person pronouns across these four verses follow the expected address and are not iltifat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.anchor: وضمائر الخطاب الأحد عشر الواقعة في الآيات الأربع من قوله : { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهادا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r11.claim: The passage shifts from life's supports to means of livelihood, including production and travel for trade; the relative noun is repeated as before.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r11.anchor: هذا الانتقال من الاستدلال والامتنان بخلق وسائل الحياة إلى الاستدلال بخلق وسائل الاكتساب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r1.claim: أزواج is plural زوج: each member of a pair is the other's partner; it commonly means male and female livestock and extends to kinds or classes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r1.anchor: والأزواج : جمع زوج ، وهو كل ما يصير به الواحد ثانيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r2.claim: Either paired animals or classes can be meant; livestock benefit people through milk, wool, hair, meat, and offspring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r2.anchor: وفي أزواج الأنعام منافع بألبانها وأصوافها وأشعارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r3.claim: For livestock, ما تركبون refers to camels used for travel; scripture names their sea-travel counterpart and Arabs call camels ships of the land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r3.anchor: فالمراد ب { ما تركبون } بالنسبة إلى الأنعام هو الإبل لأنها وسيلة الأسفار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r4.claim: جعل fits ships because they are made, while livestock are already understood as created by خلق الأزواج; human thought enables people to devise ships and train animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r4.anchor: مراعاة لأن الفلك مصنوعة وليست مخلوقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r5.claim: Ships precede livestock because pairs did not include them; naming livestock after pairs would repeat, so ships introduce a fresh gift and make livestock a newly anticipated topic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r5.anchor: وقدم الفلك على الأنعام لأنها لم يشملها لفظ الأزواج فذكرها ذكر نعمة أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p172/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur compares the sequence to Imru al-Qays: after pleasure-riding a horse he mentions embracing a woman, not riding a war horse, since the rides differ.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r1.claim: ركوب literally means mounting an animal; it extends to boarding a ship by likening ship motion to a mount's motion, hence direct transitivity with animals but في with ships.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r2.claim: من الفلك والأنعام explains the relative ما; its connected accusative relative pronoun is omitted, a common ellipsis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r2.anchor: بيان لإبهام { ما } الموصولة في قوله : { ما تركبون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r3.claim: Though riding takes animals directly and ships with في, direct transitivity is generalized because the objects are clear; the omitted pronoun follows that generalization.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r3.anchor: فغلبت التعدية المباشرة على التعدية بواسطة الحرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r4.claim: The verb تركبون is used both literally for livestock and figuratively for boarding ships.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r4.anchor: واستعمال فعل { تركبون } هنا من استعمال اللفظ في حقيقته ومجازه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.claim: These descriptions of God's acts are blessings to humanity and proof against every disbelieving polytheist.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.anchor: على كل كافر مشرك بالله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r2.claim: Al-azwaj means kinds or varieties of every thing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r2.anchor: الأزواج الأنواع من كل شيء، ومن في قوله: من الفلك للتبعيض،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r3.claim: Min in min al-fulk is partitive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r3.anchor: من في قوله: من الفلك للتبعيض، وذلك أنه لا يركب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r4.claim: Among livestock, only camels are ridden; horses, mules, and donkeys are included by the broader meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r4.anchor: وذلك أنه لا يركب من الأنعام غير الإبل، وتدخل الخيل والبغال والحمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r6.claim: Ma denotes the kind of mount ridden, and the pronoun in ظهوره refers back to that kind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r6.anchor: وما في قوله: ما تركبون واقعة على النوع المركوب، والضمير في: ظهوره عائد على النوع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r6.claim: The created pairs include all kinds of plants, crops, fruits, flowers and other growth, as well as animals of varied genera and species.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r6.anchor: أي: مما تنبت الأرض من سائر الأصناف، من نبات وزروع وثمار وأزاهير، وغير ذلك [أي] (2) من الحيوانات على اختلاف أجناسها وأصنافها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r7.claim: Ships and livestock are made compliant and usable for people to ride, eat their meat, and drink their milk.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r7.anchor: أي: ذللها لكم وسخرها ويسرها لأكلكم لحومها، وشربكم ألبانها وركوبكم ظهورها؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r3.speaker: أبو لاس الخزاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r3.claim: Abu Las reports the Prophet said every camel has a devil on its hump, so riders should invoke God's name, tame it for their needs, and remember God is the one who carries them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r3.anchor: أبي لاس الخزاعي قال: حملنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على إبل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r1.claim: The narrator called Abu Las is identified as Muhammad ibn al-Aswad ibn Khalaf.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r1.anchor: أبو لاس اسمه: محمد بن الأسود بن خلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r2.claim: A parallel report says every camel has a devil on its back; riders should say God's name and then pursue their needs without restraint.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p222/r2.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "على ظهر كل بعير شيطان

BURSEVI:v8p272/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272/r1.claim: Pairs means every class of created thing; nothing lies outside God's creation, as 36:36 says of plants, people, and unknown things.
BURSEVI:v8p272/r1.anchor: {مما تنابت الارض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون} (يس : 36) لا يشذ شيء منها عن إيجاده واختراعه

BURSEVI:v8p272/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272/r2.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v8p272/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses pairs as kinds, such as sweet and sour, white and black, male and female.
BURSEVI:v8p272/r2.anchor: الأزواج : الضروب والأنواع كالحلو والحامض والأبيض والأسود والذكر والأنثى.

BURSEVI:v8p272/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272/r3.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v8p272/r3.claim: Another view says everything besides God is paired in contrasts; this contingency shows that its creator is one, without counterpart or rival.
BURSEVI:v8p272/r3.anchor: وقيل : كل ما سوى الله فهو زوج كفوق وتحت ويمين وشمال وقدام وخلف ، وماض ومستقبل

BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r1.claim: The phrase covers what people ride by sea and land: rakiba takes livestock directly but needs a preposition with ships.
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r1.anchor: ما تركبونه في البحر والبر على تغليب أحد اعتباري الفعل لقوته على الآخر فإن ركب يعدى إلى الأنعام بنفسه

BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r2.claim: Explanation precedes what it explains to preserve the final n-sound; ships precede livestock because they show God's power and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r2.anchor: وتقديم البيان على المبين للمحافظة على الفاصلة النونية ، وتقديم الفلك على الأنعام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r1.anchor: الازواج } الأصناف { ما تركبون } أي تركبونه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r2.claim: Although Arabic says one rides livestock directly but rides in ships with a preposition, the direct construction prevails here as the stronger verb pattern.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r2.anchor: غلب المتعدي بغير واسطة ، لقوته على المتعدي بواسطة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr takes the pairs as all kinds or classes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.anchor: الأصناف كلها , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā takes them as male and female animals.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.anchor: أزواج الحيوان من ذكر وأنثى , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan lists opposites: seasons, night and day, heavens and earth, sun and moon, Paradise and Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.anchor: أن الأزواج الشتاء والصيف , والليل والنهار , والسموات والأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.claim: The pairs may be people’s alternating states: good and evil, faith and unbelief, wealth and poverty, health and illness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.anchor: أن الأزواج ما يتقلب فيه الناس من خير وشر , وإيمان وكفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.anchor: { وجعل لكم من الفلك } يعني السفن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr identifies the livestock as camels and cattle.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.anchor: في الأنعام هنا قولان : أحدهما : الإبل والبقر , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r12.speaker: معاذ
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r12.claim: Muʿādh identifies them as camels alone.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r13.claim: These blessings enable travel by land and sea.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r13.anchor: فذكرهم نعمه عليهم في تسييرهم في البر والبحر

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r3.claim: The pairs are all kinds or categories.

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r4.claim: Ships are vessels, and livestock are camels and cattle; these are things people ride.
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r4.anchor: يعني السفن، { و } من { والأنعام } يعني الإبل والبقر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r1.claim: Al-azwāj means all the kinds or categories.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r1.anchor: ﴿ والذي خلق الأزواج ﴾ الأصناف ﴿ كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r2.claim: The phrase means what you ride; since Arabic says people ride in ships and ride animals, the directly transitive usage is given precedence over the prepositional one.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110/r2.anchor: أى تركبونه يقال ركبوا في الفلك وركبوا الأنعام فغلب المتعدى بغير واسطة لقوته على المتعدى بواسطة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr interprets all the pairs as every kind or category.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أي الأصناف كلها

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r2.claim: Al-Hasan includes winter and summer, night and day, heavens and earth, sun and moon, and Paradise and Fire among the pairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: الشتاء والصيف والليل والنهار والسموات والأرض والشمس والقمر والجنة والنار

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r3.claim: Ibn Isa interprets the pairs as male and female animals.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r3.anchor: وقيل: أزواج الحيوان من ذكر وأنثى قاله ابن عيسى

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r4.claim: Another interpretation is pairs of plants, as in the verses about every beautiful pair and every noble pair.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد أزواج النبات كما قال تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r5.claim: The author prefers a comprehensive reading: all the alternating conditions people experience, including good and evil, faith and disbelief, benefit and harm, poverty and wealth, health and illness, encompassing the preceding views.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r5.anchor: وقيل ما يتقلب فيه الإنسان من خير وشر، وإيمان وكفر، ونفع وضر، وفقر وغنى، وصحة وسقم. قلت: وهذا القول يعم الأقوال كلها

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r6.claim: Here al-fulk means ships and al-an'am means camels, which people ride on land and sea.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r6.anchor: { وجعل لكم من الفلك } السفن { والأنعام } الإبل { ما تركبون } في البر والبحر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the livestock intended here are camels and cattle.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r9.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: الأنعام هنا الإبل والبقر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r10.speaker: أبو معاذ
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r10.claim: Abu Muadh says livestock here means camels alone; al-Qurtubi calls this correct and cites a prophetic report about a rider on a cow.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r10.anchor: وقال أبو معاذ: الإبل وحدها وهو الصحيح لقوله عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r11.claim: A man riding a cow hears it say that it was created for plowing, not riding; the Prophet affirms the cow, as do Abu Bakr and Umar, though they were not present among the people.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r11.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «آمنت بذلك أنا وأبو بكر وعمر»

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains “pairs” as kinds and varieties, such as sweet and sour, white and black, and male and female.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس الأزاج الضروب والأنواع كالحلو الحامض والأبيض والأسود والذكر والأنثى

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r2.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r2.claim: Some careful scholars say everything other than God is paired: above and below, directions, past and future, substances and attributes, and the seasons.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r2.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين كل ما سوى الله فهو زوج كالفوق والتحت واليمين واليسار والقدام والخلف والماضي والمستقبل

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r3.claim: Being paired shows that created things are contingent in themselves, originated, and preceded by nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r3.anchor: وكونها أزواجا يدل على كونها ممكنة الوجود في ذواتها مخدثة مسبوقة بعدم

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r4.claim: God alone is absolutely one, exalted above counterpart, rival, opposite, or helper; the creator of pairs is therefore not Himself paired.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r4.anchor: فأما الحق سبحانه فهو الفرد المنزه عن الشد والند والمقابل والمعاضد

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r5.claim: Arithmetic's first argument for the superiority of the odd or unit: a pair needs two units, whereas the unit is independent of the pair; self-sufficiency is superior to need.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r5.anchor: أن أقل الأزواج هو الإثنان وهو لا يوجد إلا عند ، حصول وحدتين فالزوج يحتاج إلى الفرد

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r6.claim: Second, an even number divides into equal parts while an odd one does not; division is passivity, whereas indivisibility signals strength and resistance.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r6.anchor: الزوج يقبل القسمة بقسمين متساويين والفرد هو الذي لا يقل القسمة وقبول القسمة انفعال وتأثر

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r7.claim: Third, dividing an odd number yields one even and one odd part, so it contains both types, whereas both halves of an even number are even.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r7.anchor: العدد الفرد لا بد وأن يكون أحد قسميه زوجا والثاني فردا فالعدد الفرد حصل فيه الزوج والفرد معا

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r8.claim: Fourth, paired counterparts share their perfections, so neither is absolutely perfect; the lone one has a perfection exclusive to itself.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r8.anchor: إذا كان كل ما حصل له من الكمال فمثله حاصل لغيره لم يكن هو كاملا على الإطلاق ، أما الفرد فالفردية كائنة له خاصة لا لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r9.claim: Fifth, paired things share some features and differ in others, making each contingent and needy; pairhood is the source of dependence, while oneness is independence and self-sufficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170/r9.anchor: فكل زوجين فهما ممكنا الوجود لذاتيهما وكل ممكن فهو محتاج فثبت أن الزوجية منشأ الفقر والحاجة

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r1.claim: Ships carry people on sea journeys and livestock on land journeys.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r1.anchor: السفر إما سفر البحر أو البر ، أما سفر البحر فالحامل هو السفينة ، وأما سفر البر فالحامل هو الأنعام

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r2.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the masculine form through the relative pronoun “what,” with the implied sense “what you ride.”
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة التذكير لقوله ما والتقدير ما تركبون

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says “backs” is plural because it is attributed to a singular collective with plural meaning, as in army or host.

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r4.claim: A third explanation is that the feminine is not a true grammatical gender here, so forms may vary, as in “among the women, one who agrees with you.”
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r4.anchor: أن هذا التأنيث ليس تأنيثا حقيقيا فجاز أن يختلف اللفظ فيه كما يقال عندي من النساء من يوافقك

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r5.claim: The verse uses the direct transitive verb for riding both animals and ships because the construction without a preposition is stronger and therefore predominates.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر الجنسين فكيف قال تركبون

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.claim: The pairs refer variously to all animal species, all opposites, or male and female members of animal kinds.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.anchor: refers to all species of animals (IK, Q), to all opposites (R), or to the fact that all animals have both males and females (Q).

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that pairs show created things are relative and multiple, whereas their Creator is Absolute and transcends duality.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.anchor: According to al-Rāzī, that they are pairs indicates that they are all relative and multiple

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.claim: Seafaring and cattle are blessings; cattle serve riding and transport, warmth and clothing, food and drink, and beauty as signs of God's beneficence.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.anchor: mention seafaring as a blessing bestowed by God (cf. 14:32; 17:66; 22:65; 30:46) and invoke the benefits of cattle

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.claim: Muslims commonly use this supplication when traveling by land; for sea travel, they are advised to use the prayer in 11:41.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.anchor: The supplication given at the end of this verse is often employed by Muslims when traveling by land

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.claim: Acknowledging that creation is made subservient to people, though they are not its equal, admits people cannot use these resources without Divine Aid.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.anchor: human beings do not have the capacity to make use of these resources without Divine Aid

TAB-FULL:v20p556/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r1.claim: Allah created all things in pairs, making males from females as pairs and females from males as pairs.
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r1.anchor: ومن الأنعام ما تركبونه في البر إلى حيث أردتم من البلدان، كالإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

TAB-FULL:v20p556/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r2.claim: Al-fulk means ships and al-anʿām means livestock; these include beasts of burden.
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r2.anchor: ومن الأنعام ما تركبونه في البر إلى حيث أردتم من البلدان، كالإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

TAB-FULL:v20p556/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r3.claim: People ride ships for travel and livelihood and ride land animals, including camels, horses, mules, and donkeys, to reach their destinations.
TAB-FULL:v20p556/r3.anchor: ومن الأنعام ما تركبونه في البر إلى حيث أردتم من البلدان، كالإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r6.claim: One view takes ‘all pairs’ to mean kinds of beings, including male and female, white and black, and others.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r6.anchor: قيل المراد بالأزواج أصناف الموجودات من ذكر وأنثى

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r7.claim: Another view takes it as pairs of every thing apart from God, such as above/below, right/left, and male/female.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد الزوج من كل شيء فكل ما سوى الله

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r8.claim: ‘What you ride’ means what you ride upon; the verb takes a direct object for animals but takes fī with ships, so the wording favors the animal construction.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r8.anchor: والركوب إذا نسب إلى الحيوان كالفرس والإبل تعدى بنفسه

TABRISI:43:11-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r2.claim: Iqran means ability or capacity: one says “I could handle this camel” when able to manage it.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r2.anchor: الإقران الإطاقة يقال أقرنت لهذا البعير أي أطقته

TABRISI:43:11-14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r5.claim: One explanation of all pairs is male and female animals.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r5.anchor: يعني أزواج الحيوان من ذكر وأنثى

TABRISI:43:11-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:43:11-14/r6.claim: Another explanation includes animal and inanimate forms and opposites such as sweet and bitter or wet and dry.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه خلق الأشكال جميعها من الحيوان والجماد فمن الحيوان الذكر والأنثى

TABRISI:43:11-14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:43:11-14/r7.claim: Al-Hasan lists winter and summer, night and day, sun and moon, heaven and earth, and Paradise and Fire as pairs.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r7.anchor: وقيل: الأزواج الشتاء والصيف والليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والسماء والأرض والجنة والنار عن الحسن

TABRISI:43:11-14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:43:11-14/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies the livestock as camels and cattle, which people ride along with ships.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r8.anchor: والأنعام } من الإبل والبقر عن سعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:43:11-14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:43:11-14/r9.claim: Another view takes the livestock meant here to be camels.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r9.anchor: وقيل: الإبل { ما تركبون } في البحر والبر

THALABI:v8p328/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p328/r13.claim: Al-azwāj means the various kinds or classes.

THALABI:v8p328/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r14.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v8p328/r14.claim: The plural ẓuhūr is attached to the singular mā because that singular has a collective sense, like army, host, and cavalry.
THALABI:v8p328/r14.anchor: وقال الفراء: أضاف الظهور إلى الواحد لأنه ذلك الواحد في معنى الجمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16/r1.claim: The pairs encompass all kinds, varieties, and colors, including male and female.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16/r1.anchor: أي الأصناف والضروب والألوان والذكر والأنثى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r3.claim: The created pairs are the various kinds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r3.anchor: والذي خلق الأزواج } الأصناف { كلها }. وقوله:

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r14.claim: Azwāj is explained as the kinds and classes of things, or universally as all contraries.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r14.anchor: Burada “ezvâc”, eşyânın envâ‘ve esnâfı veya ale’l-umûm mütekābilât ile tefsir edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r15.speaker: bazı muhakkıkīn
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r15.claim: Some verifying scholars, as al-Rāzī transmits, say everything besides God is paired, while God alone is singular and without opposite or equal.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r15.anchor: Râzî’nin naklettiği vechile bazı muhakkıkīn demiştir ki: Allah’ın mâsivâsı hep çifttir, yalnız Hak teâlâ zıdd u misilden münezzeh ferddir.

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r16.claim: The author proposes that things are paired as mental and external forms; God is not bounded by a mental form, knows Himself immediately, and is absolutely unique, unlike anything (42:11).
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r16.anchor: her şey sûret-i zihniye ve hâriciyesi itibariyle çifttir. Yalnız Hak teâlâ, sûret-i zihniye ile tahdid olunamaz. Onun kendisine ilmi de husûlî suret ile değil, huzûrîdir.

MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.claim: The masculine agreement in ‘what you ride so that you may settle on its backs’ follows the masculine relative pronoun mā.
MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.anchor: «والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون لتستووا على ظهوره» (12- 13) التذكير ل «ما»

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:13/r1.claim: Benefiting from animals for riding, carrying loads, guarding, plowing, and threshing depends on their capacity to be domesticated; without it those services would be impossible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:13/r1.anchor: Eğer yüce yaratıcı hayvanlara bu kabiliyeti vermeseydi, zikredilen hizmetlerinden istifade etmek mümkün olmazdı

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r3.claim: Mā can be a relative pronoun meaning “that which.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r3.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى ' الذي ' . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في البقرة ]
